verification: VERIFICATION RUN 2026-09-14 (pruned staged tree: remote_rpi_gpio, scrape, rest, alpha_vantage, acomax, mirroring test_cpt_detect_eval run_case): 13/14 cases FAIL, and the failures are an ENGINE SEMANTICS BLOCKER, not authoring errors. Root cause: any import statement that resolves to a PACKAGE node ('from homeassistant.components import persistent_notification' — 534 modules in the real tree do this — or fallbacks landing on 'homeassistant' itself) records an IMPORTS edge onto the package, and the prohibits BFS traverses CONTAINS from there, descending into the whole subtree. Observed paths (staged tree): alpha_vantage.sensor -> IMPORTS homeassistant.components -> CONTAINS remote_rpi_gpio -> IMPORTS gpiozero; scrape.config_flow -> IMPORTS homeassistant -> CONTAINS homeassistant.components -> CONTAINS remote_rpi_gpio -> IMPORTS gpiozero; scrape.sensor -> IMPORTS scrape-pkg -> CONTAINS config_flow -> IMPORTS homeassistant -> ... -> gpiozero. Consequence: the pin baseline is 4 fires on a 5-component tree (hundreds on the real tree, 1 genuine), and any added selenium module detonates the same cascade for ADR-0004. BOTH CONSTRAINTS ARE UNENCODABLE UNDER CURRENT SEMANTICS; every case expectation below is VOID-UNTIL-FIX and encodes the INTENDED semantics (CONTAINS traversable only during pure descent from the start/seed, never after a dependency edge). Only ha-bench-gpio-removal passes today (deleting remote_rpi_gpio removes every path to the object). GOLD IS PARKED: do not score until the engine issue is fixed and this file is re-verified; sequencing per the user decision 2026-09-14 = the fix lands after the #149/#148 baseline records (ADR 018 stated-before-data protocol). Full-graph detect on the 88k-node ADG additionally remains the known >60min CPU hazard (deferred separately). BASELINE-IS-NON-ZERO design note stands: once unblocked, every case's expected_violations include the standing remote_rpi_gpio fire; probes are 'no fire beyond the baseline', not 'zero'.

cases.description: The ADR-0019-mandated remediation executed: delete all three remote_rpi_gpio module files, taking the tree to the compliant end state (the only case whose expectation is zero)
cases.grading_note: Zero violations expected: removing every gpiozero-importing module removes every subject with a dependency path to the object (structural prohibits is evidence-driven; there is no residual state). This is the strongest subject-overreach guard in the set, stronger than the pin baseline alone: any fire at all after the deletion means a constraint is matching something it should not (object suffix drift, transitive path from an unrelated module, or a leftover node from the deleted files). RUN SHAPE: the deletion must be applied to the parsed tree itself (stage a copy of the pin tree minus the three files, then run detect with an empty diff) — augment_adg only ADDS nodes for added/modified files and cannot remove deleted files' nodes, so a diff-driven run on the pin tree would carry stale remote_rpi_gpio nodes and keep firing. This mirrors the real pipeline, where the ADG is re-parsed from the post-change tree; the diff entries above document the remediation shape for that run.
